active_paradigms.idea: Exploit affine invariance by optimizing inside a fixed regular triangle with 3-fold symmetric parametrization
active_paradigms.description: The score min(triangle area)/hull area is invariant under nonsingular affine maps, so we can WLOG assume the convex hull is a fixed equilateral triangle (or hexagon) and parametrize points in barycentric coordinates. Impose exact 3-fold rotational symmetry: 12 points as 4 orbits of 3 points under 120-degree rotation plus the center, reducing the problem from 26 to ~9 free variables. Then run scipy.optimize.minimize (SLSQP or L-BFGS-B) on the soft-min surrogate of triangle areas with analytic gradients, using tau continuation. The symmetric structure drastically shrinks the search space, guarantees balanced basins, and known best Heilbronn configurations for small n exhibit such symmetry. After the symmetric optimum is found, optionally break symmetry with tiny asymmetric perturbations and re-polish with the existing greedy hill-climb to see if the symmetric point is a local max that can be escaped.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: min_area_normalized via a low-dimensional symmetric parametrization that reaches deeper optima than generic 26-D search
active_paradigms.cautions: Compute areas in the triangle's barycentric coordinates and normalize by the fixed hull area; ensure the 3-fold orbits are constructed exactly (rotation by 120 degrees about centroid) so symmetry is exact, not approximate. Keep the tau continuation schedule and final true-min polish.

active_paradigms.idea: Direct nonsmooth maximization of the true minimum area via scipy.optimize.minimize with a k-th smallest area formulation and trust-constr
active_paradigms.description: Instead of the softmin surrogate, maximize the exact k-th smallest triangle area (k=1) directly using a smooth reformulation: introduce an auxiliary variable t and constraints A_i >= t for all 286 triangles, maximizing t. Each constraint A_i >= t is smooth (after fixing orientation signs, which can be tracked and updated between iterations since flips are rare). Feed this as a nonlinear constrained program to scipy.optimize.minimize with method='trust-constr' (or SLSQP) over 27 variables (26 coordinates + t) with 286 inequality constraints. This solves the true max-min problem directly rather than approximating it, avoiding the surrogate gap entirely. Warm-start from the current best configuration and from several structured starts; re-run after orientation sign flips are detected to keep constraints valid.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: the exact minimum triangle area (primary metric) via epigraph formulation, eliminating the softmin approximation gap
active_paradigms.cautions: The abs() in the area formula is nonsmooth; track each triangle's orientation sign from the previous iterate and flip signs when a signed area crosses zero (detect via small signed-area magnitude). Use analytic Jacobians for the constraints for speed; limit maxiter to stay within the time budget.

active_paradigms.idea: Deterministic basin-hopping / multistart with scipy.optimize.basinhopping on the softmin objective
active_paradigms.description: Replace the fixed set of ~15 handcrafted starts with scipy.optimize.baseshopping (scipy.optimize.basinhopping) applied to the existing smooth softmin value-and-gradient function at a moderate tau (e.g., 0.005). Basinhopping combines random perturbation steps with local L-BFGS-B minimization and a Metropolis acceptance criterion, systematically exploring many more basins than the current fixed-start scheme within the same wall-clock budget. Use a fixed RNG seed for determinism, a temperature around 0.002 (scale of area differences between basins), and a step size around 0.05 in the 26-D space. After each accepted basin, run the existing greedy true-min polish and keep the global best. This is a single-library, single-algorithm global search that directly attacks the main weakness of the current program: insufficient coverage of the (likely highly multi-modal) landscape.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: global exploration of the configuration space to find better local optima, improving min_area_normalized beyond 0.0256
active_paradigms.cautions: Cap total iterations (e.g., niter=60 with maxiter=80 per local minimize) to respect the evaluation timeout; seed the RNG deterministically; keep the bounds by using L-BFGS-B as the local minimizer with the existing 0-1 box bounds; always polish and record the best true min area, not the surrogate value.

tried_paradigms.idea: Smooth LogSumExp global optimization with analytic gradients via scipy.optimize.minimize (L-BFGS-B)
tried_paradigms.description: Replace the coordinate-descent hill climbing with a true gradient-based continuous optimization. The objective min over 286 triangle areas is non-smooth, but a soft-min surrogate like -tau*log(sum(exp(-area_i/tau))) is smooth and differentiable, and the gradient of each triangle area w.r.t. its three vertices has a simple closed form (perpendicular directions). Use scipy.optimize.minimize with method='L-BFGS-B' (or SLSQP) on the 26 variables, maximizing the soft-min. Use a continuation homotopy: start with tau large (averaging many triangles) and progressively shrink tau toward ~1e-4 so the surrogate concentrates on the smallest triangles, re-minimizing at each stage. Run from the current best configuration and a few structured starts, keeping the best true min-area result. This escapes the plateau problem that stalls single-vertex hill climbing because gradients jointly move all points that affect the bottleneck triangles.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: min_area_normalized (primary); also reduces eval_time vs many local-search iterations
tried_paradigms.cautions: Implement the soft-min gradient analytically in numpy (vectorized over the 286 index triples) rather than finite differences to keep it fast and accurate. Clamp tau from below (~1e-5) to avoid numerical overflow in exp; use area_i/tau with max-subtraction trick. Verify the true min area after each tau stage since the surrogate can drift; keep the best true-min configuration. Keep points inside the unit square via L-BFGS-B bounds.

tried_paradigms.idea: Optimize the convex hull shape too: parametrize the region as a stretched/affine-transformed domain instead of fixing the unit square
tried_paradigms.description: The metric divides by the convex hull area of the points, not a fixed region — so the shape of the point set's own hull matters. Configurations on a long thin hull have small hull area but also small triangles; the current program clips points to the unit square, which may not be the best hull shape. Instead, optimize points freely in a larger box and let the hull be whatever it is, or explicitly try affine-stretched initial configurations (e.g., points on an elongated hexagon, a triangle-shaped hull, or a regular 13-gon hull). Since Heilbronn-type optimal configurations for small n often place most points on the boundary of a convex polygon, seed starts with 11-13 points on a convex polygon boundary (regular 13-gon, regular 12-gon + center, triangle with points distributed on its three edges) and refine. After optimization, optionally apply a global affine transformation to reduce hull area while scaling all triangle areas proportionally — the normalized score is affine-invariant per-triangle only if hull scales identically, so instead directly check whether shrinking the hull (moving hull vertices inward along normals while keeping interior points fixed relative) increases the ratio.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: min_area_normalized by jointly improving the numerator (triangle areas) and denominator (hull area)
tried_paradigms.cautions: The normalized ratio is NOT affine-invariant: anisotropic scaling changes triangle areas and hull area by the same determinant factor, so pure area-preserving linear maps leave the score unchanged — the gain comes from nonlinear repositioning (moving hull vertices inward creates slack for interior triangles). Avoid degenerate hulls (collinear hull vertices give zero hull area but also zero min triangle area). Always recompute the true ratio with scipy.spatial.ConvexHull after refinement.

tried_paradigms.idea: Simulated annealing / basin-hopping global search with move types matched to Heilbronn geometry
tried_paradigms.description: The current multi-start local search gets trapped in local optima of a highly non-convex landscape with ~C(13,3) competing constraints. Use scipy.optimize.basin_hopping (or a hand-rolled deterministic simulated annealing with a fixed seed) over the 26 coordinates with the true min-area as the energy. Design the perturbation step to be geometry-aware: (a) move a random vertex of the current smallest triangle, (b) apply a small random affine jitter to a symmetry group of points, (c) swap an interior point with a boundary point. Use an acceptance temperature schedule that anneals from accepting ~30% worsening moves down to near-zero, with several hundred iterations per start. Combine with the existing greedy polish as the local-minimizer callback so each basin-hopping step lands on a locally refined configuration. This explores fundamentally different basins than the 10 fixed structured starts.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: min_area_normalized via better global exploration; combined_score above 1.0
tried_paradigms.cautions: Keep everything deterministic: use numpy.random.default_rng with fixed seeds, not scipy's global RNG. Runtime is secondary but must stay within the evaluation timeout — budget iterations (e.g., 200 hops x 5 starts) and vectorize the 286-triangle area computation. The energy (true min area) is piecewise linear and flat in many directions, so pair annealing with the fine-grained polish to escape flat plateaus. Track the best-ever configuration separately from the annealing state.
